st: This is an oven version of the traditional earth-oven method. Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C) and put a roasting pan with [[1 cup]] water on the lowest rack.
Season the chicken, pork and lamb all over with the salt and pepper.
Line a large deep roasting tray with a double layer of wet cloths. Lay cabbage leaves on the cloth.
Put the meats in a heavy foil tray, skin-side up, and cover with a layer of cabbage leaves.
Arrange the potatoes, sweet potatoes and pumpkin on top of or beside the meat in a separate foil tray.
Cover each tray tightly with heavy foil, then lay wet cloths over the top and seal everything with another layer of foil to trap the steam.
Cook the meat for 3 to 3.5 hours until very tender. Add the vegetable tray after the first hour.
Check the chicken reaches 165°F (74°C) and the pork and lamb are well above 145°F (63°C).
Open the foil away from your face to avoid steam, rest 10 minutes and serve in big pieces.
Take the lamb out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking. Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C).
Cut small slits all over the lamb with a sharp knife and push a garlic sliver and a small piece of rosemary into each.
Rub the lamb with [[2 tbsp]] oil, salt and pepper.
Place the lamb in a roasting pan with the onions and add the water to the pan.
Roast for 20 minutes, then lower the heat to 350°F (175°C).
Toss the potatoes with [[1 tbsp]] oil and a pinch of salt and put them around the lamb.
Roast for another 1 to 1.5 hours until the lamb reads 145°F (63°C) for medium or 160°F (71°C) for well done.
Rest the lamb for 20 minutes, loosely covered with foil.
Carve into slices and serve with the potatoes and pan juices.
Heat the oven to 300°F (150°C). Draw a 8 inch circle on parchment paper and flip it onto a baking sheet.
Beat the egg whites in a very clean bowl on medium-high speed until soft peaks form.
Add the sugar one spoonful at a time, beating well after each, until the meringue is thick and glossy and no sugar grains remain when rubbed between fingers.
Fold in the cornstarch, vinegar and vanilla.
Pile the meringue within the circle, shaping it into a round with a slight dip in the center and swirled sides.
Place in the oven and lower the temperature to 250°F (120°C). Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes until crisp and pale.
Turn off the oven and leave the pavlova inside with the door closed to cool for at least 1 hour.
Whip the cream to soft peaks.
Transfer the pavlova to a plate, top with cream and arrange the kiwifruit and strawberries on top just before serving.

ing: shortcrust pastry or extra puff pastry
st: Melt the butter in a pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, for 8 minutes until browned (160°F/71°C).
Stir in [[2 tbsp]] flour and the tomato paste, then pour in the broth and Worcestershire sauce.
Simmer for 10 minutes until thick, season with salt and pepper and cool completely.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Cut pastry into 6 rounds for the bases and 6 slightly smaller lids.
Press the bases into a muffin tin or small pie tins.
Fill with the cooled mince and top each with shredded cheddar.
Cover with the lids and press edges to seal. Brush with beaten egg and cut a small slit in the top.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until puffed and golden. Cool for 5 minutes before eating.
Rinse the whitebait gently and pat dry on paper towels.
Beat the egg whites in a clean bowl until stiff peaks form.
In another bowl, mix the yolks, flour, salt and pepper into a paste.
Stir the whitebait into the yolk mixture.
Gently fold the whisked whites into the whitebait mixture so it stays light.
Melt a little butter in a large skillet over medium heat.
Spoon in portions of mixture about 3 inches wide.
Cook for 2 minutes per side until golden and set.
Keep the fritters warm while cooking the rest, adding butter between batches. Serve with lemon wedges.
Put the pork bones in a large pot with [[8 cups]] water and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil and skim off foam.
Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours until the meat is tender and falling from the bones (above 145°F/63°C).
Add the potatoes and sweet potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Mix the flour, baking powder and [[1 tsp]] salt. Rub in the butter, then stir in the milk to make a soft dough.
Roll the dough into 8 small balls with floured hands.
Drop the dumplings into the simmering broth, cover and cook for 12 to 15 minutes.
Stir in the watercress and cook for 2 minutes until just wilted.
Taste the broth and season with salt. Serve in big bowls with bread.

ing: hoki, cod or snapper, in 4 pieces
st: Cut the potatoes into chips about 0.5 inch thick. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes, then drain and dry thoroughly.
Heat the oil to 300°F (150°C) in a deep heavy pot.
Fry the chips in batches for 5 minutes until soft but not brown. Drain.
Whisk [[1 cup]] flour, the baking powder and [[1 tsp]] salt with the cold sparkling water to a smooth batter.
Pat the fish dry and dust lightly with the remaining [[0.5 cup]] flour.
Raise the oil temperature to 375°F (190°C).
Dip the fish in batter and lower into the oil. Fry 4 to 5 minutes until golden and crisp.
Fry the chips again for 3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Drain everything on paper towels, sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt and serve with lemon.

ing: peeled and sliced, for the starter
st: Make the starter 2 days ahead. Boil the potato in 2 cups water until soft, then keep [[1 cup]] of the cooled potato water and mash the potato.
Mix the potato water, mashed potato, [[1 cup]] flour and [[1 tbsp]] sugar in a jar.
Cover loosely and keep it warm for 2 days, stirring daily, until bubbly and sour-smelling.
Mix the bread flour, [[1 tbsp]] sugar, yeast and salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1 cup]] of the starter and the warm potato water and knead for 10 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for 3 to 4 hours until doubled.
Shape into a round loaf, place in a greased pan or on a tray and rise for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep brown and hollow-sounding when tapped.
Cool on a rack for 30 minutes before slicing. Serve with butter.
Heat the milk and [[1 cup]] of the cream in a pan until steaming.
Whisk the yolks with [[0.75 cup]] sugar until pale.
Slowly pour the hot milk into the yolks while whisking, then return to the pan.
Cook over low heat, stirring, for 5 minutes until it coats a spoon (170°F/77°C). Strain into a bowl.
Stir in the remaining cold cream and the vanilla. Chill for at least 4 hours.
Line a baking tray with parchment. Heat [[0.5 cup]] sugar and the golden syrup in a deep pot, stirring until dissolved, then cook without stirring until amber (300°F/150°C).
Off the heat, quickly whisk in the baking soda. It will foam up. Pour onto the tray immediately.
Cool for 30 minutes until hard, then break into small pieces.
Churn the custard in an ice cream maker, adding the toffee pieces in the last minute. Freeze for 2 hours until firm.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line two baking sheets with parchment.
Mix the oats, flour, coconut and brown sugar in a large bowl.
Melt the butter and golden syrup together in a small pan over low heat.
Stir the baking soda into the boiling water, then add to the butter mixture. It will foam.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until combined.
Roll tablespoonfuls of dough into balls and place on the trays with 2 inches between them. Flatten slightly.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown.
Cool on the trays for 5 minutes, then move to a rack. They will crisp as they cool.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and line an 8 inch square pan.
Beat the butter and sugar for 3 minutes until fluffy. Beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Stir in the flour and baking powder alternately with the milk until smooth. Pour into the pan.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely, ideally overnight.
Cut the cooled sponge into 16 squares. Chill them for 30 minutes to make them firmer.
Sift the powdered sugar and cocoa into a bowl and whisk in the melted butter and hot milk to a thin icing.
Put the coconut on a plate.
Using two forks, dip each square in the icing and let the extra drip off.
Roll in coconut and put on a rack. Let set for 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Scrub the sweet potatoes and cut them into wedges about 0.5 inch thick.
Toss with the oil, garlic powder, salt and pepper in a large bowl.
Spread the wedges in a single layer without crowding.
Bake for 20 minutes, then flip them over.
Bake for another 10 to 15 minutes until golden and crisp at the edges.
Mix the sour cream with the chives and a pinch of salt for the dip, and add sweet chili sauce if you like.
Serve the hot wedges straight away with the dip.
